# odyssey-048 (10.274–374) — review

Two passes. `t` was never touched (checked: every `t` identical before and after, unit count unchanged, concatenation reproduces the edition). Reused published units were compared with the repository-root json by script: the whole-unit repeats at 312, 325b, 336, 368, 370 and 371 match character for character; the line-level reuse at 300, 309, 343–344, 346 and 364 matches the published wording (300 with "she" for the changed speaker). Two units (315, 325a) did not match and are changed below. Speech state: 047 ends with Odysseus's answer to Eurylochus closed at 273; 048 opens in plain narration, the outer 9.2 speech stays open at 374; Hermes (281–301), Circe (320, 325–335), Odysseus (337–344) are single-quoted, marked, and opened and closed correctly in both layers (except the 325 opening, below).

Counts: 2 high, 10 moderate, 27 minor (39 changes).

Glossary otherwise: all 125 novel forms are exactly the novel list, none already in the shared glossary; every parse was read against its line(s). All 16 `__broaden__` entries are old entry whole + " · " + new reading (verified against the root glossary). No ASCII apostrophe or backtick, no line numbers, no "here" as a line pointer (οἵδ’ "this here" is the demonstrative's meaning, as in the shipped ὅδε entry). Homeric forms name their Attic equivalent where one exists.

## Findings refused

- 345 l "as I ordered" against 373 "bade" (one verb, κελεύω): the new-renderings row bars "ordered" only for 373, and 047 ships "as you ordered" for ἐκέλευες (251). Left.
- 323 i "ran in under my sword" (the object is not in the Greek): standard reading, the note says "inside the reach of the blade". Left.
- 338–341 English ends with "?" although Murray prints a full stop at 341: it is one question from 337, and the note says so. Left.
- 307 l "to long Olympus" / i "tall Olympus": the shipped μακρόν entry gives both senses; now stated in the note. Left.
- 345 / 373: l "bade" against i "urged": κελεύω "bid, urge", already the pattern at 339 ("bid"). Left.
- 316 l "the stirred drink" (no article in the Greek; second mention after 290): left, natural.
- Over-cap `__broaden__` entries θεοῦ (366), κακὸν (580), μετ (327), τί (923): old entries already at or past 230, so no compliant broadening exists; kept as the practice since odyssey-024 (readings are real and checked against the lines). Trimming the new reading would not bring them under the cap.
- ἤνοπι gloss "gleaming, flashing" against "bright" in l/i: dictionary sense, marked as uncertain; the table only bars those words as the translation.
- Remembered English: no phrase in i reads as ready-made once rebuilt from the case relations (286 was the nearest and was rebuilt).

## Open decisions

1. 315 and 325. Both validator-forced compromises would be better solved by merging units, as odyssey-036's reviewer accepted (QUESTIONS.md, 9.252): merge 314–315 (`εἷσε … ἀργυροήλου / καλοῦ δαιδαλέου· ὑπὸ δὲ θρῆνυς ποσὶν ἦεν·`, "my feet" correct, same as the unit at 364–367) and 325 (`τίς πόθεν εἰς ἀνδρῶν; πόθι τοι πόλις ἠδὲ τοκῆες;`, restoring the opening ‘). That needs joining `t` strings, which this review was told not to do. Alternatively the owner may change check 6 to ignore quotation marks. Until then the draft passes check 6 but has "her feet" at 315 (wrong referent, noted) and no opening ‘ at 325.
2. The four over-cap broadenings above (owner's cap question, QUESTIONS.md).
